objective: Audit resolved frontier cells and task history for duplicate or near-duplicate work and determine whether a minimal novelty guard is sufficient.
bottleneck: Research efficiency depends on preserving negative evidence strongly enough to redirect search.
question: Does the durable history adequately prevent repeating equivalent experiments when a frontier cell is already resolved?
observed_effect: The evidence shows a critical gap in duplicate-work prevention: R-002 (holding-period robustness) launched despite R-001 (cost-robustness) having resolved the identical momentum cell with identical signal characteristics.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the current novelty guard mechanism is sufficient to prevent equivalent experiments.
uncertainty_reduced: Partial - confirmed frontier-first selection prevents equivalent re-tests in 6 cells, but mechanism lacks explicit duplicate-avoidance checks.
next: Implement concrete duplicate-avoidance check that prevents any experiment with identical signal characteristics after a frontier cell has been resolved and qualified.
